ambient_trade.text: lamp oil in {town} going for {gold} a flask. good price if you're riding that way, just bring your own jug.
salt's gone up again in {town}. {gold} a sack and rising. want to know why? i'll tell you over a table.
reed baskets, fresh stock, {gold} the lot. lost your pack mule to the hills? come see me in {town}.
anyone forget their tent poles? i've got spares in {town} for {gold}. i'll sell them before the rain does.

encounter_trade_offer.text: ser {player}, i'm not here to fight, i'm here to sell. {gold} for the cart and the oil and we both ride home. damn fine deal.
ser {player}, i've a load bound for {town} and a fair price on it. {gold} for the passage and we're square. what do you say?
{player}, you're the only one i'd sell to at a loss. call it {gold} and we'll talk about the salt later.
{gold} gets you a safe road to {town}, and i'll not charge you for the lamp oil. that's a deal worth taking, ser {player}.

encounter_greeting.text: stand off, {player}. {persona} of {my_faction} here. i've no quarrel with you unless you're carrying bandit steel.
{player}, {persona} here, of {my_faction}. the road's been bad, so keep your hands where i can see them and we'll get on fine.
{player}! {persona} here, {my_faction} salt route. you still owe me a horse, or i owe you, I can never remember which.
morning, {player}. {persona}, {my_faction} carts. i'm headed for the coast and i'm late already, so let's keep this short and profitable.

player_raided_my_village.text: {player} burned {village}? that's not war, that's just bad trade. i'll remember the smoke when prices come back.
{player}, you burned {village} and the carts won't come near it now. was that really worth the cost?
{village} going up in smoke. good for nobody, {player}. the salt doesn't move when the roads burn.
{player}, we can still talk. you took {village} and i lost a wagon of lamp oil there. name a price for the peace.

war_declared.text: {my_faction} and {enemy_faction} at war again. salt will jump, and i'd like to know whose pockets it lands in.
war on {enemy_faction}? wonderful. every caravan just doubled its guards and my margins went with them.
{my_faction} has gone to war with {enemy_faction}. i'll keep trading with both sides, that's the only honest thing left in this business.
so {my_faction} and {enemy_faction} are fighting. fine by me, as long as the roads stay open and the tolls stay fair.

peace_made.text: peace between {my_faction} and {faction}. finally. the caravans can stop sleeping with their boots on.
{my_faction} and {faction} have signed, so the roads should open up. good news for carts, bad news for mercenaries.
word from the table: {my_faction} has made peace with {faction}. drinks are on the salt merchants tonight.
{faction} and {my_faction}, peace at last. i'll have a wagon through that road before the ink is dry.

released_by_player.text: {player} let me out and didn't ask for a ransom? that's either charity or a long game, and i don't trust either.
{player}, thanks for the release. no ransom, no hard feelings. drop by the salt road and i'll sell you something cheap.
{player} let me go with no ransom. i'll owe you one, and i always pay my debts, in coin or in lamp oil.
{player}, you didn't have to let me walk. the next caravan's on me, and the offer stays open.

beat_by_player.text: {player} beat {troop_count} of my men in the field. i'll forgive it if the bandits stop bothering my roads.
{player}, that was {troop_count} troops i'll never see again. fair fight, but i'm still sore about the wages.
{player}, you ran {troop_count} of my lads off the field. well played. now let's talk about who's buying the wagons.
{troop_count} of my men on the grass, {player}, and you're still smiling. damn fine work, and you're still not getting my salt.

whisper_beg_help.text: {player}, {enemy_faction} is at the gates of {fief}. i can pay in salt and lamp oil, name your price.
{player}, you're the only one i trust with a sword in {fief} right now. {enemy_faction} is pushing hard and my coin won't hold them.
{player}, {fief} is about to fall to {enemy_faction}. help me hold it and the next three caravans go through your roads free.
{player}, i'd not ask if the salt wasn't on the line. {enemy_faction} wants {fief}, and i'd sooner trade with you than watch it burn.

ambient_complaint.text: bandits hit another caravan on the {town} road. the tolls are up and the guards are asleep. i'm losing money by the hour.
{rival} is undercutting every salt price in {town}. either he's selling stolen goods or he's a fool. both are bad for business.
the {faction} tolls are a disgrace. two wagons lost this year and they still want a fee for the road. i'm writing a letter.
if one more bandit tells me he's 'taking a toll', i'll charge him for the privilege. salt routes are cursed this year.

ambient_chatter.text: rain on the {town} road again. my lamp oil's the only thing keeping the carts moving at night.
anyone else's axle screaming on the hill past {village}? i'm down to three wheels and a lot of hope.
that mud at {village} is worse than the bandits. i'd pay good coin for a dry road.
the map says two days to {town}, the mules say four. trust the mules.
